data.hypothesis: A block size of 64 may improve scheduling by providing more independent CTAs than the prior 128-thread candidate, particularly at larger supported sizes. The prior 128-thread candidate was slightly faster than baseline in search, but that does not establish that smaller blocks will help; added scheduling overhead or fewer warps per CTA could instead hurt.
data.notes: Only launch geometry changes; the kernel's one-thread-per-target mapping, force equations, and memory strategy remain untouched. In search, baseline-e1 was valid at 0.0018526411283622502 s and the prior 128-thread candidate was valid at 0.0018288109272952108 s, about 1.29% lower. No per-size breakdown or independent confirmation is available. The controller must validate every supported size before comparing this candidate's timings.
transformations: Set block to 64 and items_per_block to 64, keeping shared_memory_bytes at zero and preserving the launch JSON key set.
